lessons.heading: Player quick start
lessons.title: Your first session as a player
lessons.lead: By the end, you can join a table, find your character, move your token and make a roll.

chapters.title: Get in
say: Every adventure starts with getting through the door.
Your DM sends you two things: a link, and a password. They come separately. The link never carries the password.
Open the link. Check the Connection status line. It should say Connected.
Type the table password. Passwords are case-sensitive.
Press Enter Table.

chapters.title: Find yourself
say: This is your token. Your character has a row in the Party at the bottom. Your row reads "You."
Lost your token? Press the target button on your row. The map jumps to it.
Select your row to open your character card.
Click your name to rename your character.
Click a number in HP to type a new value, or drag along the bar.

chapters.title: Move
say: Drag your token to move it. Turn Snap on and it clicks to the grid.
Everyone sees the new spot when you let go.
You can also step with WASD or the arrow keys. One press, one cell.
On a phone, open Tools, then Select. Tap your token, and use the d-pad.

chapters.title: Roll
say: Press Dice to open the roller.
Click a die to add it to the tray. Click again for more of the same.
Add a modifier chip if you need one.
Pick Normal, ADV for advantage, or DIS for disadvantage. Then pick who sees it: the table, the DM, or only you.
Press Roll.
For a quick d20, use the Roll now row. One press, one roll.
Rolling real dice at the table? Press I Rolled It, and type what you got. The log marks it "by hand."

lessons.heading: DM quick start
lessons.title: Set up your table before game night
lessons.lead: By the end, you can create a private table, claim the DM seat, put a map down, invite players and check what they see.

chapters.title: Make a table
say: Every campaign needs somewhere to happen.
Real games live on a private table. It has its own passwords, and it is never cleared automatically.
Press New Table. Give it a name you'll recognise.
Choose a table password. Your players type this one.
Choose a DM password too. Whoever knows it can run the table.
Press Create Private Table.

chapters.title: Claim the DM seat
say: You arrive as an ordinary player. This card offers two next steps. Nothing on it happens by itself.
Press Enter DM mode, and type your DM password.
You can also do this any time from the Table button, top left.

chapters.title: Put a map down
say: There are three ways to get a map on the table.
If you have a map image, upload it in the DM Menu, under Maps. Lesson three covers that.
To build one here, open Build map and press Start live map.
Press Escape to leave the editor. The map stays live.
And the third way... is the fun one.
Now press G. That's the Kicked-In Door. Pick a recipe, press Generate and enter, and HeroByte builds a stocked place and moves the table there.

chapters.title: Send the invite
say: Now Invite players works, because you are the DM. It copies the link.
Later, find it in the DM Menu, under Table, then Invite.
Send the password separately. The link does not carry it.
Unless you enjoy answering "what's the password?" for the next ten minutes.

chapters.title: See what they see
say: Press Player view. You now see exactly what players see: fog from the party's vision, secret doors hidden.
You keep every DM power. Press it again to switch back.
Player view is on the computer layout.

lessons.heading: Player path 1
lessons.title: Join a table
lessons.lead: By the end, you can get into any table and know what each join-screen message means.

chapters.title: The join screen
say: Before the dice come out, you have to get in.
Use Chrome, Edge or Firefox on a computer. Phones get their own touch layout.
First, the Connection status line. It should say Connected.
Type the table password and press Enter Table.
Get it wrong and the error shows in red. What you typed stays in the field, so you can spot the typo. Passwords are case-sensitive.
On a built map with one character, the view starts on your token.

chapters.title: Switching tables, codes, forgetting
say: Belong to more than one table? A Table picker appears above the password. Choose the table, type its password, enter.
Have a code instead of a link? Paste it in the table code box, under Start or join. Then press Join.
Forget this table drops a private table from this browser's list. You'll need its code to get back.
Your browser remembers up to twelve tables. The server publishes no list of tables, so keep your codes.

chapters.title: It remembers you
say: The password is stored for that table in this tab, so a reload drops you straight back in.
If your connection blips, HeroByte reconnects for you. You'll see Reconnecting, then Re-authenticating, under the header.
In this browser, a reload or a blip brings you back as the same person. Your seat is held for you for six hours. After that, a DM needs the DM password again.

chapters.title: One tab, one device
say: One live connection per browser. Open the same table in a second tab and the older tab pauses. Press Reclaim this tab to switch back.
A different device or browser joins as a new player, with a new character.
Sometimes this browser can't prove it's still you. Then you'll see Held in another window, and your seat stays held. Try again once. If it still fails, Start a fresh session appears.
That makes you a new player. You can't get back into your old character. Use it as a last resort.

chapters.title: The Main Hall
say: Every server starts with one table, the Main Hall. It's a public test table.
Its passwords are fixed, and by default it wipes itself after an hour with nobody in it.
You'll see the public test table marker at the top while you're there. Build freely, but don't keep anything there.

lessons.heading: Player path 2
lessons.title: The table at a glance
lessons.lead: By the end, you know every part of the screen, can find your way around the map, and can chat and join voice.

chapters.title: Toolbar, map, Party
say: A quick tour of the table, before anything tries to eat you.
Along the top are two groups: Play tools, and Panels and settings. Hover any button for a tooltip.
Tools take turns. Picking one turns the last one off. Press Move, or click the active tool again, to turn it off.
The map is shared. What you change, everyone sees. What you see through the fog is yours.
The Party at the bottom has a row for every character: the party, the DM's, and any NPCs you can see.
Cards shows every card at once. Roster goes back to rows. Hide party folds it down.
The bar also holds World, and Props when your DM allows it.

chapters.title: The Table menu
say: Top left is the Table button. It shows the table's name, and a dot for your connection: green online, red offline.
It opens a menu about the table and about you. Your role is here.
Preferences are yours alone. CRT adds scanlines and a monitor frame. Sound and motion controls animation, sound effects and volume.

chapters.title: Moving around the map
say: Drag empty map space to pan. Middle-mouse drag works even with a tool active.
The wheel zooms toward your cursor.
Reset puts the view at the map's top-left corner at normal zoom. It's not the middle of the map. Or, sadly, your token.
To find your token, press the target on your row.

chapters.title: Chat and whispers
say: Open Chat and Rolls. Chat is the first tab.
Choose Everyone for table talk, or Whisper to someone for a private message. Press Send or Enter.
Being the DM doesn't let anyone read other players' whispers.

chapters.title: Voice
say: Voice works like joining a call. Press Join voice. Allow the microphone when your browser asks.
Before you join, you can see whether a call is running and how many are in it.
Mute keeps you in the call. You still hear everyone. Leave voice hangs up.
When someone talks, their portrait on their card glows in their colour and grows.
Wear headphones. It stops echo.

chapters.title: On a phone
say: On a phone the map fills the screen, with a dock of five buttons.
Party, Tools, Dice, Chat, and Reset.
Party and Chat open full screen. Close them with the X, or drag the title bar down.
Voice is at the top of Party.

lessons.heading: Player path 3
lessons.title: Your character card
lessons.lead: By the end, you can open your card and every card at once, edit your character's name and HP, add a portrait and token art by upload or by link (and know the limits of each), set conditions and size, recolour your token, save the character to a file, and add a second one.

chapters.title: Open your card
say: Every hero needs a name, a face, and a place to count the bruises.
The Party lists characters, not players. Select your row and your card opens beside the rows.
X or Escape closes it. Select another row to switch.
Cards shows every card at once.

chapters.title: Name, HP and temp HP
say: Click the name to edit it.
Click either HP number to type a new value. Enter or click away saves.
Or drag along the bar. It goes green, amber, red as you drop.
Temp HP is a separate pool. It's used up before regular HP.
The sword button centres the map on this character's token.

chapters.title: Portrait and token art
say: The gear opens your full settings. One window per character.
Your portrait and your token are two separate pictures.
There are two ways to add one. Upload image sends a picture from your computer to the table: a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, up to five megabytes.
Or paste a link and press Apply. Links work from Imgur and Discord. Other sites are blocked, so if a link shows nothing, download the picture and upload it.
Clear takes the token back to a plain square in your colour.

chapters.title: Conditions and size
say: Status Effects is a checklist of conditions. Up to three show on your portrait and token. The rest roll into a plus bubble.
Token Size runs from Tiny to Gargantuan.

chapters.title: Your token on the map
say: Every token wears its name and, when you're allowed the numbers, a thin health bar.

Your colour is yours alone: no other player can take one close to it. Pick it in settings. Drag the handle and let go, or tap a dashed ring for a free one. The striped patches are the other players' colours, and the handle stops at their edge.
Double-click your token for a random colour nobody else is using. With a picture on it, the colour still shows in your name on the card and the ring on your Party row.
With Transform, click a token for scale and rotate handles.
A lock badge means the DM pinned it. No one can move it until they unlock it.

chapters.title: Save, load, add a character
say: Save character downloads this character to a file. Load character brings it back, here or at another table.
It's one character, never the whole table.
One warning. A file with drawings replaces the drawings you have on the map.
Add Character gives you another one, with its own row, card, token and HP. Up to five each.

chapters.title: On a phone
say: On a phone, open Party. Tap or drag your own HP to edit it.
Edit holds the name, your colour, portrait, token size, Add Character, and the character file. Double-tap your token for a new colour.
Token art is set from a computer. The phone keeps the art you gave it there.

lessons.heading: Player path 4
lessons.title: Roll dice
lessons.lead: By the end, you can build any roll, choose who sees it, enter physical dice, and roll initiative.

chapters.title: Build and roll
say: Sooner or later, everything comes down to the dice.
Press Dice for the roller. Chat and Rolls holds the history.
Click dice to add them to the tray. Nothing rolls yet. Click again for more of the same.
Click the count badge to type an exact number.
Add a +1 or -1 chip. Click a chip to type any value.
Press Roll. Each die shows, then the total.
A natural 20 gets a critical banner.
A natural one, a fumble.

chapters.title: Advantage and who sees it
say: Advantage rolls the first die twice and keeps the higher. Disadvantage keeps the lower. The other die stays, struck through.
Table means everyone. DM means you and the DM. Me means only you.
The line under the buttons says who will see it. A natural 20 only you can see is a very lonely natural 20.
A hidden roll is never sent to anyone else. Their browser has no copy.

chapters.title: Quick rolls and macros
say: The Roll now row rolls straight away: d20, advantage, disadvantage and 2d6.
Build any roll and press Save to name it and keep it.
Saved rolls live in this browser. They don't follow you to another device.

chapters.title: Rolling real dice
say: Rolling physical dice? Press I Rolled It and type the total. The tray can be empty.
Already rolled in the app, but the real dice said something else? Press That's Not What I Rolled.
Either way the log marks it "by hand." When you correct a roll, the app's number stays, struck through.
Your DM can turn hand entry off.

chapters.title: Initiative
say: Press Init on your card. Init is short for initiative: you roll it to find your place in the coming battle.
Set your modifier, then press Roll d20 now. The server rolls it, and it lands in the log with your name.
Or press Enter a roll by hand, and type your real d20.
If no fight is running, setting initiative starts combat for the whole table.
Prev and Next move the turn. Prev means previous: it steps the turn back one. On your turn, your card says Your Turn.

chapters.title: On a phone
say: On a phone, Dice opens a full-screen roller. Tap outside the result card, or its cross, to close it.
Initiative is Init on your row in Party.

lessons.heading: Player path 5
lessons.title: Draw, measure and ping
lessons.lead: By the end, you can draw and erase, place an area template, measure a distance and ping a spot.

chapters.title: Draw
say: Every battle plan needs a picture, or at least a very confident arrow.
Press Draw. The toolbox runs Tool, then Settings, then History.
Pick Freehand, Line, Rectangle or Circle. Rectangle and Circle can be filled.
Settings has colour, stroke width and opacity.
A drawing reaches everyone when you finish the stroke.
Press Move in the header to put the toolbox away.

chapters.title: Undo and erase
say: Undo and redo affect only your own drawings. Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y work while Draw is on.
Erase drawings cuts through a freehand line. Other shapes go whole. All of it. At once.
You can erase your own drawings, and old ones with no owner. The DM can remove anyone's.

chapters.title: Area templates
say: For spells, use the area templates: Burst, Cone, Cube and Bolt.
Drag out from the point of origin. It snaps to whole squares.
When you let go it's labelled with its size, like 15 ft cone. Everyone sees it. Including whoever is standing in it.

chapters.title: Measure
say: Press Measure. Click a start point, and a line follows your cursor with the distance.
Click again to freeze it. A third click starts fresh.
The whole table sees your line while you draw it, with your name on it.
Distance follows the table's diagonal rule, set by the DM.

chapters.title: Ping
say: Ping plants a coloured burst with your name, for three seconds, with a chime.
You can also double-click empty map space, in any tool.

chapters.title: On a phone
say: On a phone, open Tools, then Draw. Hide controls makes room on the map. Your tool stays on.
The small row keeps undo, redo, cancel and done.
Double-tap empty map to ping.

lessons.heading: Player path 6
lessons.title: Fog, doors and what you can see
lessons.lead: By the end, you understand fog of war, sight limits, remembered areas and doors, and can read the world map.

chapters.title: Fog follows your tokens
say: The dark is where all the interesting things hide.
When your DM runs a built map, fog of war hides what your characters can't see.
Vision comes from your own tokens. Walls and closed doors block it.
Move, and your view moves with you.

chapters.title: Sight limits
say: Your DM can give a token a sight limit, like a torch or darkvision.
Past it you see nothing, even down an open corridor.
There's no player control for this. Ask your DM. Nicely.

chapters.title: Places you have been
say: Somewhere you've already seen stays dimly lit, so you can find your way back.
It's only a memory of the ground. Anything that walked in since is still hidden.
Dim means remembered. Not safe.
The memory lives in your browser, for this table and this map.

chapters.title: Doors
say: Click a door to open or close it. Everyone hears it.
A small gold square marks a locked door. Only the DM can open those.
Secret doors exist. Until the DM reveals one, it's a wall to you.
When your DM turns the light down, the map darkens, and torches and braziers glow. That's only the look. It doesn't change what you can see.

chapters.title: The world map
say: World opens your campaign map: every place your party has found.
"You are here" marks where you're standing.
Door and stair sprites on a map lead somewhere else. Your DM opens them, and the whole table travels together.

lessons.heading: DM path 1
lessons.title: Create a private table
lessons.lead: By the end, you can choose between the Main Hall and a private table, make one, find it again, and change its password.

chapters.title: Main Hall or private table
say: Every campaign needs a home.
Every server starts with the Main Hall. It's a public test table. Its passwords are fixed, and it wipes itself after an hour empty.
For a real game, make a private table. It has its own passwords, and it's never cleared automatically.
Anyone can make one. You don't need to be a DM.

chapters.title: The NEW TABLE form
say: Press New Table.
A name helps you find it in your list later.
The table password is what your players type. Six characters or more.
The DM password is optional, eight or more. If you skip it, the first person to enter DM mode sets it.
Press Create Private Table. You get a random table code, and you arrive as an ordinary player.

chapters.title: Finding it again
say: Back on the join screen, the Table picker lists your tables by name.
Your browser remembers up to twelve. The server keeps no public list, so note your table's code.
Forget this table removes it from this browser. You'll need the code to return.

chapters.title: Keeping a Main Hall build
say: Built something good on the Main Hall? Copy it to a table of your own.
In the DM Menu, open Table, then Security, then Save as a Private Table.
Give it a name and passwords, and press Save and Go There.
Everything comes across: the map, tokens, NPCs, drawings and images. The Main Hall carries on as before.

chapters.title: Changing the password
say: On a private table, Security has Change table password. People already in stay. New joiners need the new one.
Change it if a code leaks, or after a one-shot.
Reset to default gives your table the Main Hall's password. Anyone with your code could join. Don't use it to tidy up.
Sure, it looks tidier. It also leaves your front door wide open.

lessons.heading: DM path 2
lessons.title: Become the DM and invite players
lessons.lead: By the end, you can enter and leave DM mode, invite players safely, and remove a player who has left.

chapters.title: Enter DM mode
say: Someone has to sit behind the screen, and today it's you.
DM mode belongs to the table, not a character. It's in the Table menu.
Press the Table button, top left. Under Your role, press Enter DM mode, and type the DM password.
A wrong password keeps the dialog open, with the reason, and you stay a player.
After five wrong tries, the server locks it for fifteen seconds.

chapters.title: First DM on a new table
say: This table was made without a DM password. So the first try offers to set one.
You become the DM the moment it's saved.

chapters.title: What you get
say: Two new buttons in the header: Build map, the live editor, and Player view.
The DM Menu sits at the right of the Party bar. It has six tabs.
On a phone, the dock's Reset slot becomes DM.
The Table menu now has Table settings, which opens the DM Menu on its Table tab.

chapters.title: Invite players
say: Invite players on the next-steps card stays greyed until you've been the DM. Clicking it harder doesn't help.
Now it works.
Any time later, DM Menu, Table, Invite. You'll see the table's code and Copy invite link.
The link carries no password, on purpose. Send the password another way.
On a plain local network address, the browser blocks copying, so the link shows in a box to copy by hand.

chapters.title: Who is at the table
say: Players at this table lists everyone who has joined, with a token count.
Select All grabs every unlocked token a player owns.
Remove appears on a player who isn't at the table. It clears their seat, characters and tokens. A locked token stays, and passes to you. There's no undo.
It's not a ban. The password still lets them back in, as a new player.

chapters.title: Stepping down, co-DMs
say: Leave DM mode steps you back to player. You keep your character. The password brings the tools back.
Share the DM password with a co-DM, a second Dungeon Master, and you can both hold DM powers.

lessons.heading: DM path 3
lessons.title: Three ways to get a map on the table
lessons.lead: By the end, you can put your own map image on the table, start a live map to build by hand, generate a place mid-session, and know when to use each.

chapters.title: Which one, right now?
say: There are three ways to get a map down. Bring your own art. Build it here. Or kick in a door and let HeroByte make one.
You can switch between them mid-session.
One rule ties them together. Fog and the Kicked-In Door need a live map. A picture on its own isn't one. However lovely it is.

chapters.title: A: a map you already have
say: Open the DM Menu, then Maps. Everything we need is under Current table map.
Under Map Background, upload your image. It's stored with your table.
You can paste a link instead, but the image's host must allow it. If nothing appears, download it and upload.
Now match the grid. Open Advanced. A new map starts locked, so nobody drags it mid-fight. Press Map Locked to unlock it.
In the Grid Alignment Wizard, press Start Alignment. Click two opposite corners of one square on the image. Press Apply Alignment.
Set Square Size in feet. Then lock the map again.

chapters.title: B: build it here
say: For a scene that matters, build it. Walls block sight, doors open, fog reveals the room.
Open Build map and press Start live map. The live badge lights up.
Lesson four builds a room from here.

chapters.title: C: kick in a door
say: The party goes somewhere you never prepped. They always do.
Close the editor, click the map, and press G.
The panel has a name already filled in. Type a better one if you like.
Pick the recipe. Dungeon, or a building: a tavern, shop, warehouse or house. Pick a size.
Press Generate and enter, or Enter. Reroll only changes the seed.
Seconds later the whole table is somewhere new. Fog is on, and the party stands inside the entrance.
A door sprite leads back. Click it, confirm, and the old scene comes back as you left it.

chapters.title: Mixing them
say: Want fog on your own art? Upload it, start a live map, and draw only walls and doors over it.
Walls are invisible to players, so your art shows through.
A kicked-in place is an ordinary map. Stay in the editor and change it.
Every map can join your campaign tree on the World tab.

lessons.heading: DM path 4
lessons.title: Build your first room live
lessons.lead: By the end, you can start a live map, draw a walled room with the floor and walls you want, fix mistakes, and check what players see.

chapters.title: Start a live map
say: Every dungeon starts with one room.
The map editor runs on the live table. Players see each edit the moment you make it.
Press Build map, then Start live map.
That makes a fresh map and binds it to the table. The live badge lights up.
You'll see "saving" flicker just below it as each edit lands.
The tools are grouped: Terrain, Structures, Objects, Lighting and Generate.

chapters.title: Pick a floor and walls
say: In Structures, pick Room.
The brush deck picks the floor. Choose a shelf, or search by name.
Wall ring picks the wall style: none, stone, brick, timber or dark.
None leaves the wall band unpainted, but the room still blocks sight.

chapters.title: Drag out the room
say: Drag a rectangle. The preview shows the real floor, and a size in cells.
Let go. You get floor, a wall band, and blocking walls all round.
That whole room is one step to undo.

chapters.title: Undo, redo and Escape
say: Undo map and Redo map sit above the settings. Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y work too.
Each drag is one step.
Mid-drag, Escape cancels it. Press Escape again, with nothing in progress, to leave the editor.
The map stays live. Open Build map again and you carry on.
One edit goes at a time. If you draw while the last one is still saving, you'll see "Still saving the last change." Draw it again. Nothing was half-applied.
Think of it as building one brick at a time.

chapters.title: What your players see
say: Here's the player's screen. The room appeared as you built it.
Players don't see walls. They act through fog and movement.
To check from your side, press Player view. You keep building while it's on.

lessons.heading: DM path 5
lessons.title: Walls, doors and fog
lessons.lead: By the end, you can add walls and doors, set doors locked or secret, turn on fog, and make a dungeon dark.

chapters.title: Walls
say: Good walls make good secrets.
Wall draws one straight blocking wall. Drag from point to point.
Players never see walls. They stop movement and sight.
While you edit, walls show as a see-through overlay. Pin walls overlay keeps it after you leave.

chapters.title: Doors
say: Door: leave a gap in your wall, then drag the door across the gap. The drag sets its length and angle.
Doors start closed.
At the table, anyone can click a door to open or close it.

chapters.title: Locked and secret
say: To change a door, pick it with Select, and open Inspect. Choose its state, then press Save changes.
Closed, Open, Locked or Secret.
A locked door shows a small gold lock to players, and a click tells them it's locked. You can still open it.
A secret door is invisible to players. You see it as a dashed seam.
At the table, Alt click a door to cycle its lock. Alt click a secret door to reveal it.

chapters.title: Turn on fog
say: Fog of War is in the DM Menu, under Maps. It needs a built map with walls and doors.
Players then see only what their tokens see. You still see everything.
Things outside a player's sight are never sent to them.

chapters.title: Make it dark
say: Table Sight Default sets how far every token sees. Set thirty feet and a corridor becomes something to walk down.
A single token can have its own Sight Radius, in its Token settings. 30, 60 or 120 feet, Blind, or any number you type.
A token you set yourself always wins over the table default.

chapters.title: Check it
say: Player view shows the table through the party's eyes. Fog, hidden doors, no DM overlays.
Use it while you prep. It's the difference between "I think that's hidden"... and "it is."

lessons.heading: DM path 6
lessons.title: NPCs and the token library
lessons.lead: By the end, you can add NPCs one at a time or as a pack, use the library, hide and reveal them, and set their stance.

chapters.title: Add an NPC
say: A world is only as good as the things living in it.
Open the DM Menu, then NPCs and Monsters. Press Add NPC.
Each NPC has a name, HP, temp HP, an initiative modifier, a portrait and token art.
Players can't rename, damage or move your NPCs.

chapters.title: Place it and find it
say: Place on Map drops its token at the map's top-left corner. Not the middle of your view. It hasn't vanished. It's sulking in the corner.
Press Focus to jump to it, then drag it where you want.
Pressing Place again moves it back to the corner as a fresh token. It doesn't add a second one.

chapters.title: A pack at once
say: Set the number field to five, and the button says Add five NPCs. Five arrive, numbered.
A second batch carries on the numbering. It doesn't repeat it.
Duplicate copies one NPC: HP, art, size, stance. It takes the next free number.

chapters.title: The library
say: Library opens the bundled pack: two hundred and forty-four tokens, monsters and townsfolk.
Narrow it with Monsters or Townsfolk, then Family.
Search matches every word. "Goblin archer" finds the goblin archer.
Click a token and it arrives as a new NPC, with its name, art and portrait filled in, at the right size. It isn't on the map yet. Press Place on Map, as before.
The number field works here too.

chapters.title: Hide, stance and mimics
say: Select an NPC's row for its card. The eye hides it from players. Prep an ambush hidden, reveal it on the pounce.
Stance is Enemy, Neutral or Ally. It sets the card's colour. Players see it.
Mimics come in pairs. Place the closed chest. When they touch it... press Reveal Mimic.

chapters.title: Your own tokens
say: The This Table shelf holds your own tokens. Add your own, from your computer or an image link.
Give it a name, tags and a stance, and it searches like the pack's tokens.
Players never receive the shelf.

lessons.heading: DM path 7
lessons.title: Run your first combat
lessons.lead: By the end, you can set up an encounter, get initiative from NPCs and players, run turns and end the fight.

chapters.title: The Encounter tab
say: Steel is drawn, and the dice are out.
Fights live in the DM Menu, under Encounter. Prepare, roll, run and end, all here.
Setup lists everyone who can fight: In the order, and Not rolled yet.
Monster HP players see: Exact, Bloodied, or Hidden. The server enforces it.

chapters.title: Players roll first
say: Watch one thing. Any initiative saved while no fight is running starts combat, on that character's turn.
Your players press Init, short for initiative, on their card, and roll for their place in the battle.
The first one to roll starts the fight.

chapters.title: Roll the NPCs
say: Roll missing NPC initiative rolls a d20 plus modifier for every NPC that has none.
Each gets its own line in the log. A hidden NPC rolls into your log only.
Players may type rolls by hand if your table allows it. This line tells you whether it does.

chapters.title: Start at the top
say: The turn is with whoever rolled first, not the highest roll. Yes, even if that was a goblin.
Encounter shows a note when the turn isn't at the top.
Press Start at top of order. It moves the turn there, starts the round over and refills movement.

chapters.title: Running turns
say: Next and Prev, for previous, move the turn. A chime marks each change. Anyone can press them.
The status line reads Turn, the number, and whose turn it is.
On a token's plate, its movement left this turn. Overspend and it turns red. Nothing is refused.
With monster HP on Bloodied, players see a red dot, not numbers.

chapters.title: End the fight
say: End combat stops the fight and keeps every initiative on file.
That means the next initiative anyone saves starts a new fight.
Clear all initiative empties the order.

lessons.heading: DM path 8
lessons.title: Backups and keeping your work
lessons.lead: By the end, you can download and restore a table backup, tell the three kinds of file apart, and know how big a campaign can get.

chapters.title: Three kinds of file
say: Campaigns take months to build and one bad afternoon to lose.
HeroByte makes three kinds of file, and each picker tells you which it was handed.
A table backup is the whole table. It's in the DM Menu, under Table.
A character file is one character. It's in that character's settings.
An editable map is one map. It's under Maps, in the map library.

chapters.title: Download a table backup
say: Download table backup saves the entire table as one file. Tokens, characters, NPCs, props, drawings, dice history, every saved map, and uploaded images.
Private rolls and whispers are left out.
It still holds secret doors, hidden NPCs and your notes.
Keep it to yourself.

chapters.title: Restore one
say: Restore table backup replaces the table for everyone connected. Read the confirmation.
The map, NPCs, props, drawings and settings become the file's.
Players keep their own characters and tokens. Nobody's DM status changes.
Hand it the wrong kind of file and it says so, by name, and loads nothing.
If the table would end up too big, it refuses, says why, and changes nothing.

chapters.title: How big a campaign can get
say: A backup has to restore in one go, so a table has a size limit.
The line beside the map list says where you are: Room for more maps, Nearly full, Full, or Too big to restore.
Its tooltip shows the exact size. Delete a map you're done with to make room.

chapters.title: Habits that save campaigns
say: Download a backup at the end of every session. The file name already carries the date and time.
Download one before anything risky, like mass deleting.
On free hosting, the server's disk can reset. The file in your downloads is what you can count on.
Building on the Main Hall? Save it as a private table before it clears. DM lesson one shows how.
